elements.element: Vendor must defend Customer and its affiliates.
elements.evidence: Section c expressly requires TrueLink to “defend” Client and its affiliates.

elements.element: Vendor must indemnify Customer and its affiliates.
elements.evidence: Section c expressly requires TrueLink to indemnify and hold harmless Client and its affiliates.

elements.element: Vendor’s specified defense and indemnity obligations must apply to third-party claims.
elements.evidence: Section c expressly applies to “all third-party claims.”

elements.element: Vendor’s defense and indemnity must cover claims alleging that the services or deliverables infringe intellectual property rights.
elements.evidence: Section c(i) covers allegations that the Interface, Hosting Services, Support Services, or related software or deliverables infringe or misappropriate any intellectual property right.

elements.element: Vendor’s defense and indemnity must cover claims arising from Vendor’s breach of applicable law.
elements.evidence: Section c(ii) covers any breach by TrueLink of applicable law.

elements.element: Vendor’s defense and indemnity must cover a data breach caused by Vendor.
elements.evidence: Section c(iii) covers unauthorized access to or disclosure of Client Content, Credit Data, or other Client data caused by TrueLink.

elements.element: Vendor’s defense and indemnity must cover Vendor’s gross negligence or willful misconduct.
elements.evidence: Section c(iv) expressly covers TrueLink’s gross negligence or willful misconduct.

elements.element: The indemnification procedure must require notice of the claim.
elements.evidence: Section c requires the indemnified party to give the indemnifying party written notice of any claim for which indemnity is sought.

elements.element: The indemnification procedure must give the indemnifying party control of the defense and settlement.
elements.evidence: Section c gives the indemnifying party control of the defense and settlement of the claim.

elements.element: The indemnification procedure must require reasonable cooperation from the indemnified party.
elements.evidence: Section c requires the indemnified party to provide reasonable cooperation in the defense.

elements.element: Customer’s indemnity must cover Customer-provided content.
elements.evidence: Section a(i) limits one trigger for Client’s indemnity to “the Client Content,” the operative defined term corresponding to Customer-provided content.

elements.element: Customer’s indemnity must cover Customer’s breach of law.
elements.evidence: Section a(ii) covers Client’s violation of any applicable state or federal law, rule, or regulation.

elements.element: Customer’s indemnity must contain no triggers other than Customer-provided content and Customer’s breach of law.
elements.evidence: The rendered Section a deletes the prior agreement-breach, downstream-customer, website, system-agreement, and product-injury triggers and retains only Client Content and Client’s violation of applicable law.

elements.element: Vendor must indemnify Customer against third-party claims alleging that the services or deliverables infringe intellectual property rights.
elements.evidence: Section c(i), read with the third-party-claim limitation in the opening of Section c, provides this IP indemnity.

elements.element: The Vendor IP indemnity must exclude claims arising from Customer modifications.
elements.evidence: No Customer-modification exclusion appears in the rendered clause.

elements.element: The Vendor IP indemnity must exclude claims arising from combinations with items not supplied or authorized by Vendor.
elements.evidence: No combination exclusion appears in the rendered clause.

elements.element: The Vendor IP indemnity must exclude claims arising from Customer-provided specifications.
elements.evidence: No Customer-specification exclusion appears in the rendered clause.

elements.element: The Vendor IP indemnity remedies must permit Vendor to procure the right for Customer to continue using the affected item.
elements.evidence: The rendered clause contains no procure-right remedy.

elements.element: The Vendor IP indemnity remedies must permit Vendor to modify the affected item to make it non-infringing.
elements.evidence: The rendered clause contains no modification remedy.

elements.element: The Vendor IP indemnity remedies must permit Vendor to replace the affected item with a non-infringing substitute.
elements.evidence: The rendered clause contains no replacement remedy.

elements.element: The Vendor IP indemnity remedies must provide a refund if procurement, modification, or replacement is unavailable.
elements.evidence: The rendered clause contains no refund remedy.

elements.element: Vendor’s indemnity liability must be subject to a super-cap of three times annual fees.
elements.evidence: No indemnity cap or three-times-annual-fees super-cap appears in the rendered clause.

result.reason: The rendered language fully implements the preferred position by adding the required third-party Vendor defense and indemnity triggers and procedure while narrowing Client’s indemnity to Client Content and violations of law. It does not independently satisfy the fallback because the customary IP exclusions, enumerated remedies, and 3× annual-fees super-cap are absent. The changes are confined to the indemnity allocation and preserve the remaining terms, though drafting quality is reduced by overlap between Sections b and c, the duplicated “harmless” wording in Section b, and the absence of customary settlement-consent protections.
